units.translation: How shall I address you? How shall I revere you?
How shall I speak of the end?
How do you boldly tread to the altar like a god-driven cow?
For how could one fence off the nets of ruin?
But let us share (thus Porson for κοινωσώμεθ᾽) how we might make safe plans?
How shall I weep for you?
How? How?
How shall I speak auspicious words? How shall I pray to my father?
How is it not right to repay an enemy with evils?
How then shall I, an old woman, learn from a younger one?
For how shall I hope?
For how not?
How then does he bid him come equipped?
How shall I deem these things true and alive?
How shall I accomplish it by speaking fairly?
How is it? How has it been accomplished in the house?
But how shall I escape my father's (wrathful hounds)?
How then?
How not?
For how did she nourish you?
How do you not say these things contrary to those?
For how do you defend his escape?
How, being placed by you, may I be blameless?
How will the contest be decided?
How could a bird be pure after eating a bird?
How could one who marries an unwilling woman from an unwilling father be pure?
How then do these quarrels of the kings end?
How did you dare to leave your ancestral home?
How then am I pious toward you?
How does the expense not become bitter?
But what am I to do?
How not?
How shall I speak?
Father, pity me and dear Orestes—how shall we bring them back to the house?
I wait to hear how the contest will be decided.
How is the divine power overcome?
The word is riddling; but tell me how.
how then, how indeed, how then, for how, how then, how then, how then, how not, how not
and how
somehow
how? how?
or how? Speak again, so that I may understand more clearly.
how
the word is fulfilled
but simply
somehow
somehow
wrongly ἄν πως [somehow] for ἂν πῶς [how then].
For this disease is somehow inherent in tyranny.
We have somehow already been neglected by the gods. θα. Ας.
But may it not happen somehow.
For now we wander somehow, having been sold.
A mindful (thus Hermann for ἥμενον) spirit somehow accomplished it from there, nevertheless.
And somehow perfect things are coming to me.
And to say it is easy—somehow a pollution.

The letter p lengthens the short vowel with which the preceding word ends, where the meter demands it, whether falling under the ictus or not, of which kind very many examples have been collected by Dawes Miscell. crit. p. 282 ff., Monk on Eur. Hipp. 461, Gaisford on Hephaest. vol. 2 p. 11 and others. Thus in Aeschylus Pr. 1073 διαρταμήσει σώματος μέγα ῥάκος [he will rend the great tatters of the body]. Eum. 190 ὑπὸ ῥάχιν παγέντες [pierced under the spine]. And several times in Sophocles, about which I have spoken in my Lexicon Sophocleum p. 435. Very rarely without ictus, as in the anapaestic verse of Arist. Ran. 1059
